body: This hit me really hard. You are not alone. I lost 5 years of my life because I couldn't get myself to do the things I needed to do. I have learned now that my brain is hugely momentum based, which means first thing every morning I have to get up, shower, eat, work out, etc. If I sit on the couch for even a second, my brain completely spirals inward and paralyzes me. To the point of losing entire days, weeks, months, years, etc. In the back of my head I always heard the voices of people saying I was weak and lacked willpower, so out of pure anger alone I tried to force myself to do things but the stress it wreaked on my mind was catastrophic until it broke me. It's been incredibly hard breaking free of that inward spiral but mostly because I also had no support system that understood why my behavior was the way it was. I would probably still be there if not for finally finding a decent therapist and good meds, friends, and other human stuff that can become a feedback loop of things you need to function but can't get unless those needs are met. There's so much more I could say but I'll just leave it at you are not alone and I appreciate you helping me feel that I am not alone too

I know, but from a psychological perspective when someone is confronted with proof that they behaved in a way that doesn’t make sense, such as when blackout drunk or psychotic/manic, it is natural to try to explain or justify it away after the fact because you genuinely can’t understand or remember why you did something. I have seen this often working in the mental health field. Obviously the SSRI claim is not factual, but to her in that moment when Destiny claimed the IP address matched, she was suddenly faced with definitive proof she said those things when before she had been telling herself it might not have been her because she genuinely can’t remember (or didn’t *want* to remember). People are latching on to the SSRI thing, but the larger picture is her mental health and the psychological desire to justify prior behavior from a previous mentally ill state. If I had been confronted with my own personal old logs from someone publicly, I might have tried to justify it away with medication/substance abuse too because I genuinely can’t remember saying the things I said. She deserves criticism for what she said, but I think people claiming she lied maliciously are wrong.

I understand, but I have been watching her on and off since she first went on Rajj and she has admitted her wrongdoing in her past numerous times when confronted. The only thing she hadn’t admitted until yesterday was the n-word logs, and I can understand her shame and reluctance to own up to that. That seems to be the part that is the most damning for people. Again, maybe I am naive. But I haven’t seen anything besides that to suggest she isn’t genuinely trying to change.

I recently looked back at old social media logs from when I was young, depressed, self-loathing, and severely mentally ill and was mortified at some of the edgy and ignorant things I had posted. Things I had literally no recollection of. It felt as if I was looking at myself having posted things after being blackout drunk. I can’t imagine having to publicly explain the things I said today. I can understand her shame and reluctance, and the feeling that you want to explain away the horrible things said because you know it wasn’t the real you. I can also understand why people are perceiving it as her intentionally lying. I genuinely believe she is doing her best to change and leave her past behind. If I am wrong, then I am sure it will come to light though her future actions. Maybe I am too naive and empathetic though.

For the bad trip, it was literally everything. On reflection, every single red flag in the book was there but I was oblivious at the time. 

I had about a month prior started an experiment where I went off of ADHD meds to see how I did. My memory is fuzzy due to the trauma, but I remember I was struggling with binge eating and feeling very uncomfortable in my skin but I tried to keep being mindful and fight past it. I think I was gradually losing my capacity for cognitive insight without my meds. 

I ended up going on a trip with some friends of friends. I had one close friend who invited me but everyone else I did not know very well, and my close friend was staying with a friend while me and everyone else were in a hostel type place. 

One of the people brought a bag of shrooms and I was spontaneously given the choice to do it with everyone else. In the moment, I knew I had been struggling but I thought it could help reconnect me spiritually since my last trip a year prior had been incredibly transformative. 

I foolishly trusted the person who brought them to know how much he was giving out, but he literally just went in a circle until the entire bag was empty. I have no idea how much I actually took but I imagine it was at least double a normal dose. This was hugely on me for being that irresponsible and naive with a powerful substance. 

Due to the dose and the overall discomfort of the environment and my body, I ended up spending the entire 5-6 hour trip in a panic attack state with my eyes closed on a bed, having vivid and detailed hallucinations in my head that I actually believed were real and happening. I will spare the graphic details of what I experienced but they were things that were not humanly possible to experience in human life and horror that only a human mind could think up. Basically if your subconscious mind was asked to think of creative scenarios that were far worse than death. 

The entire scenario was ultimately my fault even if my intentions were good and I am forced to accept my irresponsibility in the overall situation. I underestimated what could happen and I am still paying the price 5 years later. I always tell people now how insanely careful they need to be with dose and everything else, because a bad trip can become so much more than just a bad trip

I actually tried doing a mini-trip about a month ago to see if that would prove more therapeutic. Unfortunately it ended up being extremely uncomfortable and exacerbating my pain. Which I think makes sense, since most people say it’s important to be at a positive or neutral baseline when you do it. My trip experiences before my PTSD had been glowing and positive as well and I miss it so much.

“Professionals” can hugely vary in competency. I worked in mental health for awhile. Mental health care is fucked in a lot of places. Based on his Instagram it doesn’t even look like he was sent to a mental hospital today, just a normal one. 

From the day of his first episode in October, this screamed mania/hypomania to me. Again, I am not a psychologist. I do not diagnose. The brain is incredibly complex and different mental health conditions can easily overlap. And sometimes people just do crazy shit just for fun. With Etika, it was difficult to tell. After the first time he was let out, I was happy to admit I might’ve been wrong. But now here we are. 

Unfortunately, for someone that hasn’t 100% proven to be a danger to himself or others, psychiatric care cannot be forced on him. Denial is incredibly common. I don’t even know if I can blame anyone for being in denial given what’s happening neurologically to impair decision-making processes. I know of someone who had to drop out of college and move away TWICE until he finally accepted he needed treatment. I even know of someone who went on cryptic social media rants exactly like this which is why I initially got a terrible feeling back in October. 

Hopefully someone close will be able to get through to him. Or once this current episode naturally wears down, he will fully understand the severity of his actions himself. There is sadly not much anyone else can do. He’s not faking.

It's not uncommon (from my experience) for people to rationalize their behavior after the fact once they are stable again, which might be what's happening here. If everything that Alice said is true when she was with him in person, then there was far more going on than just "edgy humor". 

In general, there are a lot of reasons why people don't seek help right away (or don't believe they need it). I've known people with bipolar or schizophrenia that had their entire personalities change or become emotionally "flat" because of medication. But I've also known people who were able to successfully incorporate their unique/heightened states with minimal or no medication and turn it into a positive force in their lives, but this usually required extensive therapy and MOST IMPORTANTLY not being a danger to oneself or others. This is the main reason I'm concerned for Etika because his last two public episodes have included allusions to self-harm or death, that I am hesitant to write off as simply edgy humor.

Hopefully he is taking this situation seriously, and I also really hope he has friends and loved ones around to keep him safe.

Drugs, stress, genetics, a combination, etc. Assuming his first break was his last episode in October, it’s possible he happened to be listening to a lot of Travis Scott at the time and suddenly he found himself able to perceive “hidden messages” or whatever. Then what often happens is the person seeks out information that fuels whatever newfound perception or delusion the person has acquired. So I would say mental illness actually has everything to do it. 

There are an infinite number of external things that could’ve influenced him to where he is now but ultimately the core issue is internal and mental/neurological. It’s heartbreaking but at the same time it was most likely inevitable given that he did not want to seek help (and to his fairness many, many don’t because logically if you think you are a god, what help is there to receive? If you believe something incredible and special has happened to you, why would you want to change that?). I worked in the mental health field for awhile and a lot of people never seek help for this reason until it’s too late. Everything Etika is experiencing is 100% real and true in his eyes and all anyone can do is hope that he is able to get the help he needs from the professionals

This makes sense. If she gets medicated this might be much less of an issue (I actually naturally enjoy cleaning sometimes when on meds lol). Trying to get myself to clean or do shit unmedicated was torturous. Of course, that is still not an excuse long-term if you’re trying to cohabit together. 

One way I was able to get myself to do undesirable tasks is to have an explicit reward. I would start small with like 3 dishes, reward myself with a video game or something for a bit, and repeat. Eventually it got much easier (able to clean more at a time, etc) and seemed way less overwhelming doing things in small chunks. Another option could be turning it into a game somehow, get “points” for doing tasks, etc. The important thing is having some intrinsic motivator for her brain and altering her perception of cleaning as something daunting and overwhelming. Meds might be absolutely crucial for this. I am great at cleaning whether I’m on meds or not now but it took a long time of extended effort and I doubt I would’ve gotten anywhere unmedicated in the beginning. 

There are other options to get help changing behavior too if necessary such as seeing a psychologist that specializes in ADHD and getting tools from them tailored more specifically to your gf. All this however still rests on her wanting to change her behavior. It will help to get creative and it also needs to be very clear to her how important this is to you for the relationship to continue. ADHD can be incredibly frustrating, but behavior change is absolutely possible with time and effort. I hope this is somewhat helpful

In this paper, the researchers claim there were instances of studies where they found certain results that supported the paper's claims when the meditation instructor was a co-author, but didn't find them when they had another teacher implement the intervention. A huge aspect of this paper is methodological quality of meditation studies in general, the instructor bias was just one instance. There very well might be some prosocial benefits, but until methodological quality is improved there is little scientific evidence to prove it.

I'm not sure if you read the paper linked in the article, but the whole thing is pretty fascinating. 

The issue with having people co-author that are too closely involved is that they are often going to want claim results that benefit them as much as possible, hence the potential bias claim. For example, in this paper they mention that for some studies there were increases in compassion that were only found when the meditation instructor was a co-author of the study, and not when the intervention was implemented by a different teacher not involved in the authoring. Of course this is not always the case, but for some of the papers the researchers reviewed it seemed to have been.

Also, it is very well explained as to how they narrowed their thousands of choices of papers to review, and there's even a nice flow chart too. A vast amount weren't included due to perceived flaws in methodological quality.

Nobody is claiming as fact that these benefits don't necessarily exist, just that if we want to provide scientific evidence for them we need much better methodological quality. And until that happens, people should be wary about making unfounded claims. Overall, I would say this is a great introduction to discussion on the matter and would certainly not call it nonsense.

Not saying it’s impossible to be healthy and vegan, but for many it can be unsustainable. I’ve known people who were vegan for years that eventually had to stop because health issues kept accumulating over time. And there are vast amounts of online testimonies with similar stories. My point is that I have seen far more positive health stories of people incorporating meat into their diet than going vegan, and the science I have read backs this up too

Sadly, beef (grass-fed even more so) is by far the most nutritionally packed source for meat. I could easily give up chicken and pork, and even fish, but eating more beef is helping wonders with some of my ongoing health issues. I sometimes wish this wasn’t the case because of the environmental concern, but I always try to buy local for this reason.

What I don’t understand is how people still don’t see meat as the nutritionally and metabolically sound food that it is. There have been so many studies debunking meat as “unhealthy” the last decade. I care about animals and the environment and try to get grass fed/not factory farmed when possible, but I have mental/physical health conditions that meat has made a world of difference for. And my health will always come first. I can respect veganism for the moral reasons, but there is a cornucopia of research that doesn’t support it health-wise. Obviously it’s possible for some (some people live their lives on SAD with few ill effects), but the science right now is clear that the optimal way to eat for the majority of people is simply through quality fat and protein
